docs.title: Ella SMSC
docs.text: Ella SMSC lets private cellular network subscribers send and receive SMS messages. It is an SMS Service Center (SMSC) that integrates with 4G and 5G core networks.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• SMS over NAS: phones on 4G and 5G send and receive SMS through the MME or SMSF of the core over SGd.
  • SMS over IP: phones registered with an IP-SM-GW, such as Ella IMS's, send and receive SMS through it.
  • Store and forward: messages wait while a phone is unreachable, are retried, and go out as soon as the HSS says it is back, within their validity period.
  • Application messages: send messages to phones from the web UI, the HTTP API, or SMPP 3.4 for SIM OTA platforms and other ESMEs.
  • Delivery visibility: every routing lookup and delivery attempt is recorded, with why it failed.
  • Single sign-on: users log in with your identity provider, such as Google, Microsoft or Okta, over OpenID Connect.
  • Secure: users with roles, API tokens, HTTPS, and audited reads of message content.
  • Scalable: serve SMS to up to 100,000 subscribers.
  • Highly available: deploy Ella SMSC as a high-availability cluster to ensure continuous operation with failover capabilities.
  • Easy to operate: a single binary with an embedded database and configurable retention, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics. Install with snap, Docker or Kubernetes.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
These explanations provide context on how Ella SMSC works.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Ella SMSC is a Short Message Service Centre (SMSC) for private 4G and 5G networks. It stores the short messages sent to the network's subscribers, and delivers them when their phones can receive them.

Ella SMSC is a single application, with an embedded database, an embedded web UI, and an HTTP API.

docs.title: How phones send and receive SMS
docs.text: A phone exchanges SMS with Ella SMSC in one of two ways: over NAS, through the core network, or over IP, through the IMS.

docs.title: SMS over NAS
docs.text:
SMS over NAS

With SMS over NAS, the message travels inside the signalling the phone already exchanges with the core network to attach and stay registered. It needs no IMS.

docs.title: SMS over IP
docs.text:
SMS over IP

With SMS over IP, the phone sends and receives its messages as SIP messages through the IMS. An IP Short Message Gateway (IP-SM-GW) in the IMS converts between SIP and short messages, and connects to Ella SMSC. Ella IMS includes an IP-SM-GW.

docs.title: Store and forward
docs.text:
1. Ella SMSC stores the message, and acknowledges it to the sender.
  2. It asks the HSS where the recipient is served: an MME, an SMSF or an IP-SM-GW.
  3. It sends the message there.
  4. If the phone is unreachable, the HSS records that a message waits, and alerts Ella SMSC when the phone is back. Ella SMSC also retries after the retry intervals.

Messages to a phone are delivered one at a time, in order.

A message ends delivered, failed, expired at the end of its validity period, or replaced by a later message. See Statuses.

docs.title: Messages from applications
docs.text:
Besides phones, applications can send messages to subscribers, for example notifications, one-time codes or updates to SIM cards. Ella SMSC offers them two interfaces:

  • The Messages API: Ella SMSC's HTTP API, for applications you write or script.
  • SMPP: the standard SMSC protocol, for software that already speaks it, such as OTA platforms.
OTA SIM delivery with SMPP

docs.title: 3GPP roles
docs.text:
Ella SMSC integrates all three 3GPP functions:

Function Role Diameter procedures (TS 29.338) SC, Service Centre Stores each message until it is delivered or expires. SMS-IWMSC Receives the messages phones send (mobile originated, MO), and the HSS's alerts. MO-Forward-Short-Message, Alert-Service-Centre SMS-GMSC Finds where a phone is served, and delivers messages to it (mobile terminated, MT). Send-Routing-Info-for-SM, MT-Forward-Short-Message, Report-SM-Delivery-Status

docs.title: High Availability
docs.text:
A high availability (HA) cluster is several Ella SMSC nodes acting as one service centre, with one service centre address. Every node accepts short messages from phones over Diameter, from ESMEs over SMPP, and from users over the API and UI. Messages, users and settings are shared by every node.

The cluster uses the Raft consensus algorithm. A message is acknowledged to its sender only once a majority of the nodes have stored it, so an acknowledged message survives the loss of any minority of them.

docs.title: Failure tolerance
docs.text:
A cluster keeps working as long as a majority of its voting nodes are up.

Voters Failures tolerated 1 0 3 1 5 2

Ella SMSC keeps an odd number of voters, at most 5. Other nodes are standbys, promoted when a voter fails. We recommend 3 or 5 nodes.

docs.title: Diameter peers
docs.text: Each node has its own Diameter host, and they share the realm and the service centre address. Any node receives messages, and the leader delivers them. Connect each Diameter peer to every node, or connect them all through a Diameter routing agent.

docs.title: ESMEs
docs.text: An ESME binds to any node. Its limit of 4 sessions applies across the cluster. Delivery receipts and SIM answers go out through its receiver sessions, on whichever node they are bound.

docs.title: Failover
docs.text: When the leader fails, the other nodes elect a new one within a few seconds. Until then, Ella SMSC answers new messages with a temporary error, so the sender retries, and delivers nothing.

docs.title: Draining
docs.text: Draining a node prepares it for an upgrade or removal: it closes its SMPP sessions, and hands over the leadership. It keeps its Diameter connections and its vote.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text: Upgrade one node at a time, one version at a time. The cluster moves to the new version's database once every node runs it. Downgrades are not supported.

docs.title: Disaster recovery
docs.text: If a majority of the voters are lost for good, the cluster stops accepting messages. Restore the last backup on a new cluster. See Back Up and Restore.

docs.title: Users and roles
docs.text:
Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role: Admin, Read Only, Network Manager or Submitter. The role decides what the user can see and do, from reading settings to managing other users. See Roles.

The first user, an Admin, is created when Ella SMSC is initialized. Admins create the others.

Ella SMSC limits login attempts, from each address and for each account, to slow down password guessing.

docs.title: Single sign-on
docs.text: Users can also log in through the organization's identity provider. See Single sign-on.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
Applications, such as an OTA platform, use an API token rather than a password. A token belongs to a user and has that user's role, but it cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users. Tokens can expire, and an Admin or the token's user can delete one at any time.

Give each application its own Submitter user: it can send messages, and read only the messages it sent.

docs.title: ESMEs
docs.text:
An ESME, such as an OTA platform, binds to the SMPP listener with a system_id and a password. SMPP 3.4 limits that password to 8 characters, so Ella SMSC adds other checks:

  • Each ESME acts as a user, whose role decides whether it may submit or receive.
  • An ESME binds only from the networks in its allow-list. An empty list allows no address.
  • Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes. A password the SMSC generates has 8 random letters and digits.
  • Binds are limited from each address, and wrong passwords for each ESME. Every refused bind gets the same answer, so a client cannot tell which check failed.
  • Only an Admin, logged in rather than with an API token, creates, changes or deletes ESMEs.

SMPP 3.4 has no encryption: the password and the messages cross the network in clear. TLS, with smpp.tls, is a common convention outside SMPP 3.4, which the ESME must support. Use plain TCP only over a private link, such as an IPsec VPN, or in a lab.

The allow-list checks the address of the TCP connection. Terminate TLS in Ella SMSC itself, not in a proxy or load balancer, which would hide the ESME's address. On Kubernetes, the Service keeps it with externalTrafficPolicy: Local.

docs.title: Message content
docs.text: Messages carry personal content. Reading it is a permission of its own: a Read Only user sees that messages were sent and delivered, but not what they say. Every read of the content is recorded in an audit event, with who read it and from where.

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text: Ella SMSC serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in api.tls (see the configuration file). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

docs.title: Diameter peers
docs.text:
Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that connects and supports S6c or SGd, and its Diameter connections are not encrypted. Keep its Diameter address on a network that only the core network can reach.

Through an edge agent, other networks can send short messages to Ella SMSC, which does not filter them by realm. Have the edge agent accept only the operator's roaming partners.

docs.title: Single Sign-On
docs.text:
Users can log in to the UI through the organization's identity provider instead of, or as well as, a password. Ella SMSC works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity, Google or Keycloak. To set it up, see Configure single sign-on.

Login page with single sign-on

docs.title: Password and single sign-on
docs.text:
Password Single sign-on Credentials kept by Ella SMSC The identity provider, with its own policies, such as multi-factor authentication Role set by An Admin An Admin, or the user's groups at the identity provider Session 30 days The session lifetime, 24 hours by default Access removed by Deleting the user in Ella SMSC, at once Removing the user at the identity provider, at the end of their session

Password login stays when single sign-on is on, and at least one Admin always keeps a password. An identity provider that is down or misconfigured cannot lock everyone out.

docs.title: Matching users
docs.text: A user is matched to their account at the identity provider, not to their email address, so a changed or reused email address does not give access to another user. The email address is used once, to link the account at its first login, and only if the identity provider has verified it. A provider that does not say whether email addresses are verified, such as Microsoft Entra ID, must be trusted explicitly: anyone who can set their email address there could take over the matching user. An account with no user in Ella SMSC gets one only from a group mapping.

docs.title: Offboarding
docs.text: Ella SMSC does not learn when someone is removed at the identity provider. Their session lasts until its lifetime ends, and their API tokens until deleted. A shorter session lifetime narrows that window, at the cost of logging in more often. To end access at once, offboard the user in Ella SMSC.

docs.title: Client secret
docs.text: The identity provider's client secret is stored in the database, and so in its backups.

docs.title: Back Up and Restore
docs.text: A backup holds message content, user accounts, and the single sign-on client secret. Store and transfer it encrypted.

docs.title: Back up
docs.text:
1. Create an API token for an admin: in Users, open the user, and in API Tokens, click Create Token.

  2. Download a backup:

    curl -OJ http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/backup \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."

    This saves smsc-backup-<time>.tar.gz. In a cluster, back up from any node.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. Log in as an admin, and keep the token:

    TOKEN=$(curl -s http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "admin@example.com", "password": "..."}' | jq -r .result.token)

  2. Restore the backup:

    curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/restore \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \
  --data-binary @smsc-backup-<time>.tar.gz

    In a cluster, restore on any node.

docs.title: Disaster recovery
docs.text:
Use this procedure when a cluster lost a majority of its nodes, or a standalone node was lost.

  1. Install Ella SMSC on a new host, as in Install. For a cluster, add a cluster block to the configuration file.
  2. Open http://<host-ip>:5010 in a browser and initialize it with a temporary user.
  3. Restore the backup with that user, as in Restore.
  4. For a standalone deployment, stop here.

  5. Log in with a user from the backup, and add the other nodes, as in Deploy a High Availability Cluster, steps 2 to 4. Delete the data of any node that was in the old cluster first:

    sudo snap stop ella-smsc.smscd
sudo rm -rf /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db* /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/raft
sudo snap start ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: Configure Single Sign-On
docs.text: This guide lets users sign in to the Ella SMSC UI through an OpenID Connect identity provider. It gives the steps for Keycloak; other providers are set up the same way.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: served over HTTPS, at a URL with no path.
  • Identity provider: an OpenID Connect provider, reachable from Ella SMSC over HTTPS.
  • Ella SMSC account: an Admin that signs in with a password.

The examples use these values:

Value Role https://smsc.example.com Ella SMSC's external URL https://smsc.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback Redirect URL: the external URL followed by /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback

docs.title: 1. Register Ella SMSC at the identity provider
docs.text:
KeycloakOther providers

In the realm users sign in to:

  1. Go to Clients and click Create client.
  2. Set Client type to OpenID Connect and Client ID to smsc. Click Next.
  3. Turn on Client authentication. Keep Standard flow checked. Click Next.
  4. Set Valid redirect URIs to the redirect URL. Click Save.
  5. In the client's Credentials tab, copy the Client Secret.

In Users, turn on Email verified for each user.

  1. Register a web application, or confidential client, with the redirect URL.
  2. Create a client secret for it.
  3. Allow the openid, email and profile scopes.

If the provider does not send email_verified, turn on Trust email addresses from this provider in step 2.

docs.title: 2. Configure Ella SMSC
docs.text:
In the UI, go to Single Sign-On and, in Provider, click Edit. Set:

Field Value External URL https://smsc.example.com Issuer URL Keycloak: https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm>. Otherwise, from the provider. CA certificate The PEM CA certificate of the identity provider, only if a private CA signs its certificate Client ID Keycloak: smsc. Otherwise, from the provider. Client secret The secret from step 1 Display name The name on the login button, such as Keycloak Scopes openid email profile Session lifetime 24 hours, or less to end access sooner after offboarding Trust email addresses from this provider Off, unless the provider does not send email_verified

Check that the Redirect URL under the external URL is the one registered in step 1.

docs.title: 3. Test the identity provider
docs.text: In the dialog, click Test. Fix the issuer URL or the CA certificate until it shows Works. Click Update.

docs.title: 4. Enable single sign-on
docs.text:
On the Single Sign-On page, click Enable.

To turn it off, for example during an incident, click Disable. Everyone who logged in with single sign-on is signed out.

docs.title: 5. Sign in
docs.text:
1. Give a user access: create their user, or map their groups to a role.
  2. In a private browser window, open https://smsc.example.com, and click Log in with your display name.
  3. Sign in at the identity provider. Ella SMSC opens.

If the login page shows an error, the auth_oidc_login audit event in the logs gives the reason.

docs.title: Connect through Diameter Agents
docs.text: This guide connects Ella SMSC to an edge agent (DEA), to deliver short messages to roaming subscribers, and to a DRA in front of the HSS.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: integrated with its core, as in Integrate with a Third-Party Core.
  • A user with the Network Manager or Admin role.
  • The agents: their Diameter hosts and SCTP addresses. Each has Ella SMSC's host, realm and Diameter address as a peer.
  • The visited networks: support SMS in MME (SGd), or an SMSF with a Diameter host and realm.

The examples use these values:

Value Role dea1.ipx.example.net, 192.0.2.10, 198.51.100.10 Edge agent dra1.example.net, 10.3.0.20 DRA in front of the HSS epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org Ella SMSC's realm

docs.title: 1. Add the edge agent
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter and click Add Peer:

  • Host: dea1.ipx.example.net
  • Addresses: 192.0.2.10, 198.51.100.10, every SCTP address of the agent.
  • Port: 3868

Click Add Route, and keep Application set to SGd and Destination to Default. Click Add.

To add a backup agent, repeat with its host and addresses, and set the route's Priority to 1.

When an agent fails with a message in flight, Ella SMSC sends the message through the backup, and the subscriber may receive it twice.

docs.title: 2. Add the DRA
docs.text:
Skip this step if the HSS connects to Ella SMSC.

Click Add Peer:

  • Host: dra1.example.net
  • Addresses: 10.3.0.20
  • Port: 3868

Click Add Route, and set:

  • Application: S6c
  • Destination: Realm
  • Realm: epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org

Click Add.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
On the Diameter page, under Configured Peers:

  • Each agent shows open. Hover over another state to see why.
  • The DRA shows HSS set to yes.

Send a short message to a roaming subscriber. On the Messages page, it shows delivered.

docs.title: Deploy a High Availability Cluster
docs.text: Ella SMSC can be deployed as a high-availability cluster to provide redundancy and failover capabilities. See High Availability for more information.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Three hosts meeting the standard system requirements.
  • Ella SMSC installed on each host via the Install guide, with a cluster block in the configuration file.

docs.title: 1. Start node 1
docs.text: Start node 1, open a browser at the API address and initialize it normally.

docs.title: 2. Create a join token for node 2
docs.text: Still in node 1, open the Cluster page, click Add Node, click Create Token, then copy the token.

docs.title: 3. Start node 2
docs.text: Start node 2, open a browser at the API address and click Join an existing cluster instead. Paste the token and click Join.

docs.title: 4. Add node 3
docs.text: Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node 3.

docs.title: 5. Connect the Diameter peers
docs.text: Connect every Diameter peer, such as Ella Core, the HSS or Ella IMS, to every node, with each node's address and Diameter host. The Cluster page lists each node's Diameter Host. Or connect the nodes and the peers through a Diameter routing agent, as in Connect through Diameter Agents.

docs.title: 6. Verify
docs.text: On the Cluster page, all three nodes appear as Healthy.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Choose one of the installation methods below.

Snap (Recommended)SourceDockerKubernetes

Install the Ella SMSC snap:

sudo snap install ella-smsc

Configure Ella SMSC:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml

Start Ella SMSC:

sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd

Install the required dependencies:

sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc

Clone the Ella SMSC repository:

git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc.git
cd smsc

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella SMSC:

go build -o smsc -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/smsc/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/smsc

Configure Ella SMSC:

vim smsc.yaml

Start Ella SMSC:

./smsc --config smsc.yaml

Create a new directory:

mkdir ella-smsc
cd ella-smsc

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_smsc_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/smsc.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5010
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.7

services:
  ella-smsc:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-smsc:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_smsc_config
        target: /smsc.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/smsc --config /smsc.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    stop_grace_period: 50s
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - ella-smsc-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-smsc-data:

Set diameter.address to an address of the host that the core can reach.

Start the Ella SMSC container:

docker compose up -d

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the Multus CNI installed, and the sctp kernel module loaded on its nodes.

Download the Ella SMSC manifests:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/smsc.git

Edit smsc/k8s/smsc-diameter-nad.yaml to set master to the host interface that connects to your core, and set the Diameter address. Use the same address for diameter.address in smsc/k8s/smsc-configmap.yaml.

Deploy Ella SMSC:

kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl apply -k smsc/k8s

Ella SMSC's UI and API are on the ella-smsc NodePort Service.

Ella SMSC's UI and API are at http://<host-ip>:5010. Open the UI and create the first user.

See the configuration reference for all options.

docs.title: Integrate with Ella Core
docs.text: This guide connects Ella SMSC to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS (S6c) and the MME or SMSF (SGd).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: installed and started, as in Install.

The examples use these values:

Value Role 10.3.0.7 Ella SMSC's Diameter address 001 / 01 Ella Core's MCC and MNC +15550000000 Ella SMSC's service centre address +15550001111 Ella Core's SMS number

docs.title: 1. Set the Diameter address
docs.text:
In smsc.yaml, set the address Ella Core reaches Ella SMSC on, and restart Ella SMSC:

diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7

docs.title: 2. Set the operator
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the Operator page:

  • Click the edit icon next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), enter Ella Core's MCC and MNC, e.g. 001 / 01, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Service Centre Address, enter +15550000000, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Numbering, enter your country code and prefixes, and click Update.

Go to the Diameter page and note the Host, e.g. smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org.

docs.title: 3. Add Ella SMSC to Ella Core
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to Operator and scroll to the SMS section:

  • Check that SMS Number is set, e.g. +15550001111, Ella Core's default.
  • Click Add Service Center, enter:
    • Address: 10.3.0.7
    • Numbers: +15550000000
    • Diameter Identity: the Host of step 2.
  • Click Add.

The service center shows Connected.

docs.title: 4. Give subscribers an MSISDN
docs.text: In the Ella Core UI, for each subscriber that sends or receives SMS, go to Subscribers, open the subscriber, click the edit icon next to MSISDN, enter its E.164 number, e.g. +15551230001, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Set the SMSC number on the SIM cards
docs.text: On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to +15550000000.

docs.title: 6. Verify
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers, Ella Core shows open, with HSS set to yes.

Send an SMS between two phones. On the Messages page, it shows delivered.

docs.title: Integrate with Ella IMS
docs.text: This guide lets Ella SMSC deliver SMS to phones registered for SMS over IP with Ella IMS's IP-SM-GW. Phones send SMS over IP to Ella SMSC the same way.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: connected to Ella Core, as in Integrate with Ella Core.
  • Ella IMS: connected to Ella Core, as in Ella IMS's Integrate with Ella Core.

The examples use 10.3.0.7 as Ella SMSC's Diameter address and +15550000000 as its service centre address.

docs.title: 1. Enable SMS over IP in Ella IMS
docs.text:
Follow Ella IMS's Enable SMS over IP guide. When you add the SMSC, enter:

  • Address: 10.3.0.7
  • Roles: SGd only
  • Service Centres: 15550000000
  • Transport: SCTP
  • Host: the Host of Ella SMSC's Diameter page, e.g. smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org

docs.title: 2. Verify
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers, Ella IMS shows open, with Applications set to SGd and HSS set to no.

Send an SMS to a phone registered for SMS over IP. On the Messages page, click the message: its delivery attempt went to Ella IMS's host, marked (IP-SM-GW).

docs.title: Integrate with a Third-Party Core
docs.text: This guide connects Ella SMSC to a 4G or 5G core other than Ella Core, through its HSS (S6c) and its MMEs or SMSFs (SGd).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: installed and started, as in Install.
  • HSS: supports S6c, in the realm epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org of the core's PLMN.
  • MME or SMSF: supports SGd, and gives the MSISDN of the phone in each short message it forwards. The HSS names it, in its routing answers, by the Diameter identity it connects to Ella SMSC with.

The examples use 10.3.0.7 as Ella SMSC's Diameter address, 001 / 01 as the core's MCC and MNC, and +15550000000 as Ella SMSC's service centre address.

docs.title: 1. Set the Diameter address
docs.text:
In smsc.yaml, set the address the core reaches Ella SMSC on, and restart Ella SMSC:

diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7

docs.title: 2. Set the operator
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the Operator page:

  • Click the edit icon next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), enter the core's MCC and MNC, e.g. 001 / 01, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Service Centre Address, enter +15550000000, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Numbering, enter your country code and prefixes, and click Update.

The Diameter page shows Ella SMSC's Host and Realm, e.g. smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org and epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org.

docs.title: 3. Add Ella SMSC to the core
docs.text:
In the HSS, and in each MME or SMSF, add Ella SMSC as a Diameter peer:

  • Address: 10.3.0.7
  • Port: 3868
  • Transport: SCTP
  • Host and Realm: those of step 2.
  • Application: S6c in the HSS, SGd in the MME or SMSF.

In each MME or SMSF, route the short messages of service centre address +15550000000 to Ella SMSC.

docs.title: 4. Provision the subscribers
docs.text: In the HSS, give each subscriber that sends or receives SMS an MSISDN. On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to +15550000000.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers:

  • The HSS shows open, with HSS set to yes. If it shows no, its realm differs from Ella SMSC's, or it does not support S6c.
  • Each MME or SMSF shows open, with SGd in Applications.

Send an SMS between two phones. On the Messages page, it shows delivered.

See Connectivity and 3GPP Compliance for the interfaces Ella SMSC supports.

docs.title: Manage Single Sign-On Users
docs.text: These guides manage users who sign in through the identity provider. Configure single sign-on first.

docs.title: Give a user access
docs.text:
1. In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:
    • Email: the user's email address at the identity provider
    • Password: off
    • Role: the user's role
    • Pin role: checked to keep this role, if groups are mapped to roles
  2. Click Create.

The user signs in with Log in with the display name. Their first login links their user to their account at the identity provider.

docs.title: Map groups to roles
docs.text: Users in a mapped group get their role from it at each login, and get a user at their first login. Users in no mapped group cannot sign in through the identity provider, unless their role is pinned.

docs.title: 1. Send groups to Ella SMSC
docs.text:
KeycloakOther providers
  1. Go to Clients, open the smsc client, and open the Client scopes tab.
  2. Click smsc-dedicated, then Configure a new mapper, or Add mapper > By configuration, then Group Membership.
  3. Set Name and Token Claim Name to groups. Turn off Full group path. Keep Add to ID token on.
  4. Click Save.

The groups are group names, such as smsc-admins.

Configure the provider to send the user's groups in a claim, such as groups, as a list of group names or IDs.

docs.title: 2. Map the groups in Ella SMSC
docs.text:
1. Go to Single Sign-On and, in Roles from groups, click Edit.
  2. Set Groups claim to groups.
  3. Click Add group for each group, and set the group and its role. Put the most privileged first: a user in several groups gets the role of the first.
  4. Click Update.

docs.title: Pin a user's role
docs.text:
A pinned role is kept whatever the user's groups.

  1. Go to Users and open the user.
  2. In Account, edit the role: choose the role, check Pin role, and click Update. Changing a role that comes from groups checks it for you.

To unpin, uncheck Pin role. The role then follows the user's groups from their next login.

docs.title: Unlink a user
docs.text:
Unlink a user whose account at the identity provider was replaced, so that their next login links the new account by email.

  1. Go to Users and open the user.
  2. In Account, click Unlink, then Unlink.

docs.title: Offboard a user
docs.text:
1. Remove or disable the user at the identity provider. They can no longer sign in, but their current session lasts until the Session lifetime ends.
  2. To end their access at once, go to Users in Ella SMSC, open the user, and click Delete. This also deletes their API tokens and ESMEs.

To keep the user and their ESMEs instead, open the user and:

  1. In Account, click Unlink, then Unlink. This ends their single sign-on sessions.
  2. Click Remove Password, then Remove, if they have one.
  3. In API Tokens, delete each token.

docs.title: Perform a Rolling Upgrade
docs.text: This guide walks through upgrading every node in a running Ella SMSC high-availability cluster, one at a time, without taking the cluster offline.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A running cluster deployed via Deploy a High Availability Cluster.
  • The next version of ella-smsc available.

docs.title: Upgrade one node
docs.text:
Repeat these steps for each node.

  1. Open the Cluster page on any healthy node other than the one you are about to upgrade.
  2. In the node's Node actions menu, click Drain this node. Wait until its Drain column shows Drained.

  3. On that host, refresh the snap:

    sudo snap refresh ella-smsc

  4. On the Cluster page, wait for the node to return to Healthy.

  5. In the node's Node actions menu, click Resume this node. Wait until its Drain column shows Active.
  6. Move to the next node.

docs.title: Verify the upgrade
docs.text:
After every node has been refreshed, open the Cluster page and confirm:

  • Every node's Version column shows the target release.
  • Every node is Healthy and its Drain column shows Active.

docs.title: Scale a High Availability Cluster
docs.text: This guide walks through adding a node to an existing Ella SMSC high-availability cluster, removing one, and replacing one whose database diverged.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • A running HA cluster deployed (see Deploy a High Availability Cluster).

docs.title: Add a node
docs.text:
1. Prepare a host with Ella SMSC installed per the Install guide, with a cluster block in the configuration file.
  2. Open the Cluster page on any node in the cluster.
  3. Click Add Node, click Create Token, and copy the token.
  4. Start Ella SMSC on the new host.
  5. Open the new node's UI in a browser. Click Join an existing cluster instead, paste the token, and click Join.
  6. Connect every Diameter peer to the new node, unless they connect through a Diameter routing agent.
  7. On the Cluster page, verify the new node appears and is shown as Healthy.

docs.title: Remove a node
docs.text:
1. Open the Cluster page on any node in the cluster.
  2. In the node's Node actions menu, click Drain this node. Wait until its Drain column shows Drained.
  3. In the same menu, click Remove from cluster. For a node that is down for good, check Force remove (skip drain).
  4. Disconnect the Diameter peers from the removed node.

docs.title: Replace a diverged node
docs.text:
A node whose database differs from the leader's shows Diverged in the Healthy column of the Cluster page, and increments ellasmsc_cluster_state_mismatches_total.

  1. Remove the node, as in Remove a node.

  2. On the removed node, stop Ella SMSC and delete its data:

    sudo snap stop ella-smsc.smscd
sudo rm -rf /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.db* /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/raft
sudo snap start ella-smsc.smscd

  3. Add the node back, as in Add a node, steps 2, 3, 5 and 6. It gets a new Diameter Host.

  4. On the Cluster page, verify the node is shown as Healthy.

docs.title: Send Messages from an Application
docs.text: This guide gives an application, such as an OTA platform, an API token to send messages with.

docs.title: 1. Create a user for the application
docs.text:
In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:

  • Email: an address for the application, such as ota@example.com
  • Password: any password of at least 8 characters
  • Role: Submitter

Click Create.

docs.title: 2. Create an API token
docs.text:
Open the user, and in API Tokens, click Create Token. Name it after the application, check No expiry, and click Create.

Copy the token. It is not shown again.

docs.title: 3. Configure the application
docs.text:
Send a message with the token:

curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from": "+15550001000", "to": "+15551230002", "text": "hello"}'

See the Messages API.

docs.title: Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over SMPP
Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over SMPP
docs.text: This guide connects an OTA platform to Ella SMSC over SMPP 3.4 with TLS, sends a secured packet to a SIM with submit_sm, and receives the SIM's answer and a delivery receipt as deliver_sm.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella SMSC: installed, as in Install.
  • A TLS certificate for the SMSC, smpp.pem, with its chain, and its private key, smpp.key, in PEM.
  • A user with the Admin role, logged in to the UI.
  • The OTA platform's network: the IP prefix it connects from, such as 10.1.0.0/24.
  • The secured packet, at most 140 octets with its user data header.

The examples use 15550001000 as the source and 15551230002 as the MSISDN of the SIM.

docs.title: 1. Enable the SMPP listener
docs.text:
Copy the certificate and key:

sudo cp smpp.pem smpp.key /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/
sudo chmod 600 /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.key

In /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml, add:

smpp:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 2775
  tls:
    cert: /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.pem
    key: /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smpp.key

Restart Ella SMSC:

sudo snap restart ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: 2. Create a user for the OTA platform
docs.text:
In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:

  • Email: ota@example.com
  • Password: any password of at least 8 characters
  • Role: Submitter

Click Create.

docs.title: 3. Add the ESME
docs.text:
Go to SMPP and click Add ESME. Set:

  • System ID: ota
  • User: ota@example.com
  • Password: empty, to generate one
  • Allowed networks: 10.1.0.0/24

Click Add. Copy the generated password from the ESME Password dialog. It is not shown again.

docs.title: 4. Bind the OTA platform
docs.text:
Configure the OTA platform to bind as a transceiver, with:

Setting Value Host, port <host-ip>, 2775, over TLS system_id ota password The generated password interface_version 0x34

On the SMPP page, the Sessions of ota show Transceiver from the platform's address.

docs.title: 5. Submit the packet
docs.text:
Send a submit_sm with:

Field Value source_addr_ton, source_addr_npi, source_addr 1, 1, 15550001000 dest_addr_ton, dest_addr_npi, destination_addr 1, 1, 15551230002 esm_class 0x40, UDHI protocol_id 0x7F, (U)SIM data download data_coding 0xF6, 8-bit data, message class 2 registered_delivery 0x09: the SIM's answer and a delivery receipt short_message The packet's user data header, then the packet: 027000…

submit_sm_resp gives the message_id.

docs.title: 6. Receive the SIM's answer
docs.text:
The SMSC sends a deliver_sm with esm_class 0x50 and receipted_message_id set to the message_id. Its short_message is the SIM's Response Packet, 027100….

Answer it with deliver_sm_resp ESME_ROK.

docs.title: 7. Receive the delivery receipt
docs.text:
The SMSC sends a deliver_sm with esm_class 0x04 and receipted_message_id set to the message_id. Its short_message is the receipt:

id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:

Answer it with deliver_sm_resp ESME_ROK.

See the SMPP reference for every field, outcome and refusal.

docs.title: Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over the API
Send (U)SIM Data Download Messages over the API
docs.text: This guide sends a secured packet that an OTA platform built to a SIM, over the HTTP API, and reads the SIM's answer.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An API token of a Submitter user, as in Send Messages from an Application.
  • The secured packet, at most 140 octets with its user data header, in hexadecimal.

docs.title: 1. Send the packet
docs.text:
Send the packet as a binary message, with:

  • protocol_identifier: 127, (U)SIM data download
  • data_coding_scheme: 246, 8-bit data, message class 2
  • user_data_header: the packet's user data header, such as 027000
  • user_data: the packet after its header
curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "from": "+15550001000",
        "to": "+15551230002",
        "binary": {
          "protocol_identifier": 127,
          "data_coding_scheme": 246,
          "user_data_header": "027000",
          "user_data": "<packet>"
        }
      }'

Note the id of the message in the response.

docs.title: 2. Wait for the delivery
docs.text:
Get the message until its status is no longer pending:

curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."

docs.title: 3. Read the SIM's answer
docs.text:
Get the content of the message:

curl http://<host-ip>:5010/api/v1/messages/<id>/content \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ellasmsc_..."

The SIM's answer is the user_data of the last item of deliver_reports. See Get the Content of a Message.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
This section provides detailed reference material for Ella SMSC, from configuration options to complete API documentation.

  • API
  • Configuration File
  • Observability
  • Connectivity
  • SMPP
  • Performance
  • System Requirements
  • 3GPP Compliance

docs.title: 3GPP Compliance
docs.text:
Ella SMSC implements the 3GPP SMSC of TS 23.040, with the S6c, SGd and Gdd Diameter interfaces of TS 29.338.

Note

Open an issue if you notice a 3GPP-compliance gap or require a new capability for a production deployment.

docs.title: SGd and Gdd (TS 29.338)
docs.text:
• MO-Forward-Short-Message, received: a phone's short message, from its MME, SGSN, SMSF or IP-SM-GW.
  • MT-Forward-Short-Message, sent: a short message or a status report, to the phone's MME, SGSN, IP-SM-GW, or SMSF for 3GPP or non-3GPP access.

docs.title: S6c (TS 29.338)
docs.text:
• Send-Routing-Info-for-SM, sent: the serving nodes of the recipient, for a short message or a status report.
  • Report-SM-Delivery-Status, sent: the outcome of a delivery, which sets or clears the HSS's message waiting data.
  • Alert-Service-Centre, received: the recipient, or the Alert MSISDN of its subscription, can be reached again.

docs.title: Diameter routing (RFC 6733, GSMA IR.88)
docs.text:
• Static peers. Over SCTP, multi-homed.
  • Realm routing. Per realm and application, with a default route, and Destination-Host kept.
  • Failover. By priority, with load sharing, and the T flag on retransmission.

docs.title: Short messages (TS 23.040)
docs.text:
• TPDUs. SMS-SUBMIT received; SMS-DELIVER and SMS-STATUS-REPORT sent; SMS-SUBMIT-REPORT with the TP-Failure-Cause of a refused SMS-SUBMIT.
  • Store and forward. Messages to a phone are delivered in order, one at a time, and announce the next with TP-More-Messages-to-Send.
  • Validity period. Relative, absolute and enhanced formats, including single-shot messages.
  • Status reports. On the delivery, failure, expiry or replacement of a message whose sender set TP-Status-Report-Request.
  • Reject duplicates. TP-Reject-Duplicates.
  • Replace short message. Replace types 1 to 7 of TP-Protocol-Identifier, from phones, the API and SMPP. A message replaces only one from the same submitter: a phone's, one from the same phone (TS 23.040 §2.1.1); the API's or an ESME's, one of the same user or ESME.
  • Binary messages from the API and SMPP. TP-Protocol-Identifier, TP-Data-Coding-Scheme, TP-User-Data-Header and TP-User-Data delivered unchanged, including (U)SIM data download.
  • SMS-DELIVER-REPORT. Kept from each delivery: in the SM-RP-UI of a successful MT-Forward-Short-Message answer, and in the SM-Diagnostic-Info of an SM Delivery Failure.
  • (U)SIM data download error. A message whose SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has the TP-Failure-Cause usim_data_download_error fails without another attempt.
  • SC time stamps. Distinct for the messages to a phone.
  • Numbering. International, national and unknown types of number, converted to international with the operator's numbering plan.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• SMS-COMMAND. Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause command_unsupported.
  • Telematic interworking. Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause telematic_interworking_not_supported.
  • Device triggering from phones. Refused with the TP-Failure-Cause unspecified_tp_pid_error.
  • SMSMI-Correlation-ID. A short message that carries one is refused with DIAMETER_ERROR_FACILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.
  • Diameter over TCP.
  • Delivery to an MSC-Number.
  • Destination-Host in Report-SM-Delivery-Status.
  • MAP over SS7.
  • Routing to other networks' HSSs. Send-Routing-Info-for-SM goes to the operator's realm only, not the realm of the recipient's MSISDN (TS 29.338 §5.3.1.1.2).

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
Ella SMSC is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella SMSC with the --config flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected. Changes take effect on restart.

The operator and delivery settings are not in this file: they are in the database, and set with the UI or the API.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• logging (object, optional): The logging configuration.
    • level (string, optional): The log level: debug, info, warn, or error. Default info.
  • db (object): The database configuration.
    • path (string): The path to the SQLite database file. Created if absent.
  • api (object): The HTTP API and UI.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 5010.
    • tls (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  • diameter (object): Diameter, to the HSS, MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs.
    • name (string): The network interface to listen on, on all its addresses, advertised to peers. Either name or address must be set.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on, advertised to peers. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::. Either name or address must be set.
    • port (int, optional): The SCTP port to listen on. Default 3868.
  • smpp (object, optional): The SMPP 3.4 listener for ESMEs, such as OTA platforms. Without it, Ella SMSC does not listen for SMPP. The ESME accounts are in the database, managed with the API.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 2775. Not the API's port.
    • tls (object, optional): Wrap each connection in TLS, 1.2 or later, from its first octet. SMPP 3.4 has no TLS: this is a common convention, which the ESME must support. Default: plain TCP, for a private link or a lab only.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  • cluster (object, optional): The cluster port. Required to create or join a cluster.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all addresses, with advertise set.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 7000.
    • advertise (string, optional): The host:port the other nodes reach this node at. Default address:port.
  • telemetry (object, optional): The traces.
    • enabled (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default false.
    • otlp_endpoint (string): The host:port of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when enabled is true.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
logging:
  level: info
db:
  path: smsc.db
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5010
diameter:
  address: 127.0.0.1
  port: 3868
cluster:
  address: 10.0.0.1
  port: 7000
smpp:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 2775
  tls:
    cert: /etc/smsc/smpp.pem
    key: /etc/smsc/smpp.key
telemetry:
  enabled: true
  otlp_endpoint: localhost:4317

With the snap, the configuration file is /var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml.

docs.title: Connectivity
docs.text:
Interface Peer Transport Address Port API and UI Operators, applications, Prometheus TCP api.address api.port (5010) Diameter: S6c HSS SCTP diameter.address, or the addresses of diameter.name diameter.port (3868) Diameter: SGd and Gdd MME, SMSF, IP-SM-GW over SGd; SGSN over Gdd SCTP diameter.address, or the addresses of diameter.name diameter.port (3868) Diameter: S6c and SGd, outbound Configured peers: DEA, DRA SCTP The peer's addresses The peer's port (3868) SMPP 3.4 ESMEs, such as OTA platforms TCP, or TLS with smpp.tls smpp.address smpp.port (2775) Cluster The other Ella SMSC nodes TCP, mutual TLS 1.3 cluster.address, advertised as cluster.advertise cluster.port (7000)

Defaults are in parentheses. SMPP listens only when the configuration file has an smpp block, and the cluster port only when it has a cluster block.

Ella SMSC accepts any Diameter peer that supports S6c or SGd. It connects to the configured peers, and reconnects after 1 to 30 seconds. In a cluster, every node connects to the configured peers, and every other peer connects to every node.

docs.title: Diameter identity
docs.text:
Item Value Host smsc-<id>.node.epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org Realm epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org

<MCC> and <MNC> are the operator's, with a 2-digit MNC padded to 3. <id> is the last 12 hex characters of the node ID. The host does not change for the life of the node.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Ella SMSC supports four observability pillars: Metrics, Logs, Traces, and Profiles.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Ella SMSC exposes Prometheus metrics at GET /api/v1/metrics.

Metric Type Description ellasmsc_build_info Gauge Always 1. The version and revision of the running build are in its labels. ellasmsc_messages_received_total Counter Short messages received, one per part, by origin (mobile, api, smpp) and result (accepted, rejected, error, and throttled for smpp). One per submit_sm for smpp, throttled when the inbound window is full. ellasmsc_messages_completed_total Counter Short messages and status reports that reached a final status, by type (message, status_report) and status (delivered, failed, expired, and replaced for a message). ellasmsc_messages_purged_total Counter Short messages deleted once their retention passed, with their status reports and delivery attempts. ellasmsc_messages_pending Gauge Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type and state: due, to be delivered now or being delivered; waiting, for a retry or for the phone to be reachable. Exported by the leader only. ellasmsc_message_delivery_duration_seconds Histogram Time from submission to delivery of the short messages delivered, the time the phone was unreachable included. ellasmsc_hss_peers Gauge Open peers that serve S6c in the operator's realm: HSSs, or agents in front of them. At 0, messages to phones wait. ellasmsc_peer_requests_total Counter Requests to the HSS and to the MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs, by interface (s6c, sgd) and result (success, failure, absent_user, error, timeout). ellasmsc_peer_request_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of requests to the HSS and to the MMEs, SMSFs and IP-SM-GWs, by interface. ellasmsc_smpp_sessions Gauge Bound SMPP sessions, by bind type (transmitter, receiver, transceiver). ellasmsc_smpp_binds_total Counter SMPP bind attempts, by result (accepted, rejected). ellasmsc_smpp_notifications_pending Gauge Delivery receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to an ESME and not expired, by type (receipt, sim_answer). A rise means no receiver of the ESME is bound, or it does not acknowledge them. Exported by the leader only. ellasmsc_smpp_notifications_sent_total Counter Delivery receipts and SIM answers that reached a final outcome, by type and result (acknowledged, rejected, expired, no_user_data). ellasmsc_smpp_submit_duration_seconds Histogram Time from a submit_sm read to its submit_sm_resp written. ellasmsc_api_request_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of API requests, by method, route (/api/v1/messages/{id}) and status code. Requests to /api/v1/pprof/ and to no route are left out. ellasmsc_oidc_logins_total Counter Logins through the identity provider, by outcome: success, or a login error. ellasmsc_database_query_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of database calls, the wait for the connection included. ellasmsc_database_query_errors_total Counter Failed database calls. ellasmsc_database_storage_bytes Gauge Size of the database on disk, by file: main, wal. ellasmsc_cluster_failure_tolerance Gauge Voters that can fail without stopping writes. Leader only. ellasmsc_cluster_state_mismatches_total Counter Members whose database differs from the leader's. go_* Gauge, Counter, Summary Go runtime: goroutines, heap, garbage-collection pauses. process_* Gauge, Counter Process: memory, CPU, open file descriptors, start time. raft_* Gauge, Counter, Summary hashicorp/raft metrics. In a cluster only.

docs.title: Traces
docs.text:
Ella SMSC exports OpenTelemetry traces when telemetry.enabled is set in the configuration file.

Property Value Export OTLP over gRPC, without TLS Sampling Parent-based, always on for a trace the SMSC starts Propagation W3C Trace Context Delivery, SMPP and Diameter spans No MSISDN, IMSI or message content

docs.title: Spans
docs.text: Span Kind Description {method} {route} Server A request to the API, except /api/v1/livez, /api/v1/readyz, /api/v1/metrics and /api/v1/pprof/. Links to the caller's traceparent. submit_sm Server A submit_sm from an ESME. deliver {origin_host} Consumer A delivery attempt of a short message or status report, named after the Diameter Origin-Host of the SMSC. A new trace, linked to the span that created the message. deliver_sm Client A delivery receipt or SIM answer to an ESME. A new trace, linked to the span that created the message. S6c/{command}, SGd/{command} Server, Client A Diameter request.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Span Values ella.sms.delivery.outcome deliver {origin_host} delivered, failed, expired, replaced, retry, interrupted

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Ella SMSC exposes the net/http/pprof API at /api/v1/pprof/.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Ella SMSC writes its logs to standard output, one JSON object per line, at the level of logging.level in the configuration file.

Field Description ts Time of the event. level debug, info, warn or error. msg What happened. trace_id Trace ID of the span the event happened in, as 32 hex digits. Absent outside a span. span_id Span ID of the span the event happened in, as 16 hex digits. Absent outside a span. trace_flags W3C trace flags of that span, as 2 hex digits: 01 when sampled.
