docs.title: SMPP
docs.text:
Ella SMSC is an SMPP 3.4 SMSC for External Short Message Entities (ESMEs), such as OTA platforms. An ESME submits short messages to phones with submit_sm, and receives delivery receipts and SIM answers as deliver_sm.

The listener runs when the configuration file has an smpp block. ESME accounts are managed with the ESMEs API or the SMPP page of the UI.

"§" without a TS number refers to SMPP v3.4, Issue 1.2. Convention marks a behaviour that SMPP 3.4 does not define. All conventions are listed under Conventions.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: Item Value Transport TCP (§2.4), on smpp.port, default 2775. TLS With smpp.tls: TLS 1.2 or later, from the first octet. A listener is either plain or TLS. Convention. Client address The address of the TCP connection. The PROXY protocol is not supported. interface_version 0x34. SMSC system_id EllaSMSC, in bind responses. command_length 16 to 69,632 octets (68 KiB). Convention: SMPP 3.4 sets no maximum (§3.2.1). sequence_number 0x00000001 to 0x7FFFFFFF (§5.1.4).

docs.title: Supported
docs.text: PDU Direction Session state Handling bind_transmitter, bind_receiver, bind_transceiver ESME → SMSC OPEN See Binds. submit_sm ESME → SMSC BOUND_TX, BOUND_TRX One short message. See submit_sm. deliver_sm SMSC → ESME BOUND_RX, BOUND_TRX Delivery receipts and SIM answers. See Notifications. enquire_link Both Bound Answered at once (§4.11). unbind Both Bound See Session end. generic_nack Both Any Sent for a PDU that cannot be handled (§4.3). Received in answer to a deliver_sm: a temporary failure.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
PDU received Response Session command_length under 16 or over 68 KiB generic_nack ESME_RINVCMDLEN Closed sequence_number of 0 or over 0x7FFFFFFF generic_nack ESME_RUNKNOWNERR, sequence_number 0 Stays up query_sm, replace_sm, cancel_sm, submit_multi, data_sm, outbind, deliver_sm, an undefined or reserved command_id generic_nack ESME_RINVCMDID Stays up alert_notification None: discarded (§4.12) Stays up A bind in a bound state Its response with ESME_RALYBND Stays up Another request in a state that does not allow it (§2.3, Table 2-1) Its response with ESME_RINVBNDSTS Stays up A body on a PDU that has none, or a body shorter than its mandatory parameters generic_nack ESME_RINVCMDLEN Stays up A C-Octet String over its maximum length Its response with ESME_RINVPARLEN Stays up Optional parameters that do not decode as TLVs Its response with ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM Stays up A response that matches no request None: discarded Stays up

Unknown TLVs, and known TLVs not expected for the PDU, are ignored (§3.3). Responses may go out of order: they match their requests by sequence_number (§2.5.2).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
The SMSC checks a bind in this order:

  1. At most 20 binds per minute from the client address: per IPv4 address, or per IPv6 /64.
  2. interface_version is 0x34 or later.
  3. At most 100 wrong passwords per hour for the system_id, from inside its allowed networks. A successful bind resets the count. Wrong passwords from outside the allowed networks, and binds with an unknown system_id, are counted apart, with the same limit, and never lock out the account.
  4. system_id and password match an ESME account. A check against an unknown system_id takes as long as one against a known system_id.
  5. The client address is in the account's allowed_networks. An empty list allows no address.

  6. The role of the account's user allows the bind type:

    Bind Permissions Roles Transmitter Send messages Admin, Network Manager, Submitter Receiver Read messages and their content Admin, Network Manager, Submitter Transceiver Both Admin, Network Manager, Submitter

    See Roles.

  7. Fewer than 4 sessions of the account are bound.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Outcome command_status Body Accepted ESME_ROK system_id EllaSMSC, and sc_interface_version 0x34 (§5.3.2.25). Refused, any check ESME_RBINDFAIL, never ESME_RINVSYSID or ESME_RINVPASWD None. bind_transceiver_resp: system_id EllaSMSC (Table 4-6).

The log gives the reason of a refused bind, with the system_id and the client address, at level info.

docs.title: Bind fields
docs.text: Field Handling system_id Up to 15 characters (§4.1.1). password Up to 8 characters (§4.1.1). interface_version See Checks. system_type, addr_ton, addr_npi, address_range Ignored.

docs.title: Account changes
docs.text: Updating or deleting an ESME, or changing the role of or deleting its user, closes its sessions.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Item Value Sessions per ESME 4, of any bind types. ESME accounts 50. Inbound window 64 requests handled at once per session. One more is answered ESME_RTHROTTLED. §2.5.2 recommends at most 10 outstanding. Outbound window 10 deliver_sm without a response per session (§2.6.2).

docs.title: Timers
docs.text:
The timers are fixed (§7.2).

Timer Value Action session_init_timer 30 s A connection that has not bound is closed. enquire_link_timer 30 s without a PDU received The SMSC sends enquire_link, and closes the session without a response within the response_timer. inactivity_timer 90 s without a PDU received The session is closed. response_timer 30 s A deliver_sm without a response is a temporary failure.

docs.title: Session end
docs.text: Event Handling unbind from the ESME The SMSC finishes the submit_sm in progress, answers unbind_resp, waits up to 2 s for the ESME to close the connection, then closes it (§2.2, §4.2). A submit_sm received meanwhile is answered ESME_RINVBNDSTS. SMSC shutdown The SMSC sends unbind to each session, waits up to 5 s for unbind_resp, then closes.

docs.title: submit_sm
docs.text:
One submit_sm stores exactly one SMS-SUBMIT: one message of the Messages API, owned by the ESME's user, delivered as a message from the API.

submit_sm_resp carries message_id: the id of the message in the Messages API, in decimal. The SMSC answers once the message is stored.

docs.title: Addressing
docs.text:
The destination is a phone, routed through the HSS (§5.2.5, §5.2.6, §5.2.9; TS 23.040 §9.1.2.5):

dest_addr_ton dest_addr_npi destination_addr 1, international 0 or 1 The international number. 0, unknown, or 2, national 0 or 1 Converted to international with the operator's numbering plan. Error command_status Another dest_addr_ton ESME_RINVDSTTON Another dest_addr_npi ESME_RINVDSTNPI Not 1 to 20 digits, or not 1 to 15 digits without a leading 0 once international ESME_RINVDSTADR

The source is shown to the recipient as the sender (§5.2.8):

source_addr_ton source_addr_npi source_addr Sent to the phone as 1, international 0 or 1 1 to 15 digits, no leading 0 TON 1, NPI 1 5, alphanumeric Any 1 to 11 letters and digits, single spaces between words, not all digits TON 5 0, 2, 3, 4 or 6 0, 1, 3, 4, 8, 9 or 10 1 to 20 digits The TON and NPI given Error command_status Empty source_addr ESME_RINVSRCADR. The SMSC has no default source. A reserved source_addr_ton ESME_RINVSRCTON Another source_addr_npi ESME_RINVSRCNPI. The NPIs accepted have the same value and meaning in §5.2.6 and TS 23.040 §9.1.2.5. Another source_addr ESME_RINVSRCADR

docs.title: data_coding
docs.text:
data_coding (§5.2.19) is mapped to a TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4):

data_coding SMPP 3.4 meaning TP-DCS and user data 0x00 SMSC default alphabet TP-DCS 0x00. The octets are GSM 7-bit default alphabet septets, one per octet, 0x1B for the extension table. An octet over 0x7F: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. Convention. 0x01 IA5 (ASCII) Converted to GSM 7-bit, TP-DCS 0x00, or to UCS2, TP-DCS 0x08, when a character has no GSM 7-bit equivalent. An octet over 0x7F: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0x02 Octet unspecified TP-DCS 0x04, 8-bit. 0x03 Latin-1 Converted to GSM 7-bit, TP-DCS 0x00, or to UCS2, TP-DCS 0x08, when a character has no GSM 7-bit equivalent. 0x04 Octet unspecified TP-DCS 0x04, 8-bit. 0x08 UCS2 TP-DCS 0x08, octets copied. An odd number of octets: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0xF0 to 0xF7 GSM message class control Copied. 0xC0 to 0xDF GSM message waiting indication ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0x05 to 0x07, 0x09 to 0xBF, 0xE0 to 0xEF, 0xF8 to 0xFF Other character sets, or reserved ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. SMPP 3.4 has no status for an invalid data_coding.

With a GSM 7-bit TP-DCS, the SMSC packs the septets after the user data header, with fill bits (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24).

dest_addr_subunit (§5.3.2.1, §5.2.19 note e) sets the message class bits of TP-DCS:

dest_addr_subunit Class 0, 5 to 255 Unchanged. 1, MS display Class 0 2, mobile equipment Class 1 3, smart card Class 2 4, external unit Class 3

A different class already in data_coding, or a TP-DCS without class bits: ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL.

(U)SIM data download. With protocol_id 0x7F, data_coding 0x02 or 0x04 and no dest_addr_subunit, TP-DCS is 0xF6, 8-bit data, class 2. Convention: TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9 requires class 2 for (U)SIM data download.

docs.title: esm_class
docs.text: Bits (§5.2.12) Value Handling 1-0, messaging mode 00 default, 11 store and forward Store and forward. 1-0 01 datagram, 10 transaction ESME_RINVESMCLASS 5-2, message type 0010, 0100, ESME acknowledgements ESME_RINVESMCLASS 5-2 Other Normal message (§3.3). 6, UDHI 1 TP-UDHI = 1. The user data starts with the user data header, its length octet included. A header longer than the user data: ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 7, reply path 1 ESME_RINVESMCLASS

docs.title: protocol_id
docs.text:
Copied to TP-PID (§5.2.13; TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9):

protocol_id Handling 0x20 to 0x3E, telematic interworking ESME_RSUBMITFAIL 0x41 to 0x47, replace short message types 1 to 7 Replaces the pending message of the same type, from the same source, submitted by the same ESME. A message from a phone, the API or another ESME is never replaced. Convention. 0x48, device triggering Needs an application port addressing information element, else ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. 0x7C, 0x7F Need message class 2 after the data_coding mapping, else ESME_RSUBMITFAIL. Other Copied.

docs.title: registered_delivery
docs.text:
registered_delivery (§5.2.17) asks for notifications to the ESME. It does not set TP-Status-Report-Request.

Bits Value Handling 1-0 00 No receipt. 1-0 01 A receipt on the final status. 1-0 10 A receipt on failure only: failed, expired or replaced. 1-0 11 Reserved: no receipt (§3.3). 3-2 10 or 11, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement The SIM answer. 3-2 01, SME Delivery Acknowledgement Accepted, not honoured. 4 1, intermediate notification Accepted, not honoured.

docs.title: Validity and scheduling
docs.text:
Field Handling validity_period Empty: the default validity of the delivery settings. Absolute or relative (§7.1.1): the end of the validity period. In the past or malformed: ESME_RINVEXPIRY. The SMS-DELIVER carries no validity period. schedule_delivery_time Not empty: ESME_RINVSCHED.

A two-digit year is read within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year. Convention.

docs.title: User data and optional parameters
docs.text: Field Handling short_message (§5.2.22), message_payload (§5.3.2.32) One or the other. Both: ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD. sm_length Must match short_message. 255, or a mismatch: ESME_RINVMSGLEN. User data Must fit one TPDU once mapped: 140 octets, or 160 septets, the user data header included. Else ESME_RINVMSGLEN. The SMSC does not split user data. sar_msg_ref_num, sar_total_segments, sar_segment_seqnum All three: a concatenation information element, 0x00 with a reference up to 255, else 0x08 (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24.1, §9.2.3.24.8). Not all three: ignored. A total of 0, or a sequence number of 0 or over the total: ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL. source_port, destination_port A 16-bit application port addressing information element, 0x05 (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24.4). A missing one of the two is port 0. Convention. sar_* or ports with UDHI set ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD (§5.2.12). user_message_reference Echoed in the receipt and the SIM answer. sm_default_msg_id 1 to 254: ESME_RINVDFTMSGID. The SMSC has no canned messages. replace_if_present_flag 1: ESME_RINVSUBREP. Other values: taken as 0. service_type, priority_flag, other optional parameters Ignored.

docs.title: Order of submit_sm_resp and deliver_sm
docs.text: The message is handed to delivery once submit_sm_resp is written. A notification on the message can still reach the ESME before its submit_sm_resp when another message to the same recipient is being delivered.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
When a message from an ESME reaches its final status, the SMSC queues the SIM answer, then the receipt, that the submit_sm asked for, and sends them as deliver_sm.

Item Handling Session A receiver or transceiver session of the ESME that submitted the message, the one with the fewest deliver_sm in flight. Convention. No receiving session Notifications wait until the ESME binds as receiver or transceiver. They survive a restart. Order Notifications on one message go one at a time: the receipt waits until the SIM answer is acknowledged, rejected or expired. deliver_sm_resp ESME_ROK Acknowledged. deliver_sm_resp ESME_RX_P_APPN or ESME_RX_R_APPN Rejected. Not sent again. ESME_RX_T_APPN, another status, generic_nack, or no response within the response_timer Sent again after 1 minute, then doubling, at most every hour. Session closed or unbinding during the send Sent again at once on another receiving session, or on the next bind. Expiry The default validity of the delivery settings, from the message's final status. An expired notification is not sent. ESME deleted Its notifications are dropped.

Notifications are delivered at least once. The SIM answer and the receipt of a message share its receipted_message_id, and differ by the message type of esm_class.

docs.title: Delivery receipts
docs.text:
A receipt is an SMSC Delivery Receipt (§2.11, §4.6.1, Appendix B):

Field Value source_addr_ton, source_addr_npi, source_addr The destination of the message, as submitted. dest_addr_ton, dest_addr_npi, destination_addr The source of the message, as submitted. esm_class 0x04, SMSC Delivery Receipt. protocol_id, priority_flag, registered_delivery 0. data_coding 0x01, IA5. Convention. short_message The receipt text. receipted_message_id (0x001E) The message_id. message_state (0x0427) See the table below. user_message_reference (0x0204) That of the submit_sm, when present.

The text follows the example format of Appendix B:

id:42 sub:001 dlvrd:001 submit date:2610281430 done date:2610281431 stat:DELIVRD err:000 text:
Field Value id The message_id, not padded. sub 001. dlvrd 001 for a delivered message, else 000. submit date When the SMSC received the message, YYMMDDhhmm, UTC. done date When the message reached its final status, YYMMDDhhmm, UTC. For a replaced message, when it was replaced. Convention. stat, err See the table below. text Empty. Message status stat message_state (§5.2.28) err delivered DELIVRD 2 000 expired EXPIRED 3 070, TP-Status 0x46 replaced DELETED 4 002, TP-Status 0x02 failed UNDELIV 5 The TP-Status of the failure, such as 066, TP-Status 0x42

err is the TP-Status (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15), in decimal. Convention. network_error_code is not sent.

docs.title: SIM answers
docs.text:
The SIM answer is the TP-User-Data of the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT of the last delivery attempt (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a), from the RP-ACK, or from the RP-ERROR of an SM delivery failure. For a (U)SIM data download message, it is the SIM's Response Packet (TS 31.115 §4.4; TS 31.111 §7.1.1.1).

It is sent when registered_delivery bits 3-2 are 10 or 11, for any protocol_id, as an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement (§2.11). Convention.

No SIM answer is sent for a replaced message, or when the SMS-DELIVER-REPORT has no TP-User-Data.

Field Value Addresses As in a receipt. esm_class message type 0100, SME Manual/User Acknowledgement. Convention. esm_class UDHI 1 when the report has TP-UDHI, or when the message's TP-PID is 0x7F and the user data starts with a valid user data header (TS 31.115 §4.1). Else 0. esm_class, typical 0x50 protocol_id The report's TP-PID, else the message's. data_coding See the table below. short_message The TP-User-Data, its user data header included, such as 027100…. receipted_message_id The message_id. Convention: §5.3.2.12 defines it for receipts. message_state Absent. user_message_reference That of the submit_sm, when present. Report TP-DCS data_coding short_message GSM 7-bit, or no TP-DCS (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.27) 0x00 Septets, one per octet. UCS2 0x08 The octets. 8-bit That of the submit_sm when it is 0x02, 0x04 or 0xF4 to 0xF7, else 0x04 The octets.

A SIM that rejects a (U)SIM data download message answers with an RP-ERROR whose TP-Failure-Cause is 0xD5, (U)SIM data download error. The message fails at once with TP-Status 0x42: the ESME gets the SIM answer, then the receipt stat:UNDELIV err:066.

docs.title: command_status values
docs.text:
Values the SMSC sends (§5.1.3):

command_status Value Sent in When ESME_ROK 0x00000000 Any response Success. ESME_RINVMSGLEN 0x00000001 submit_sm_resp sm_length, or user data longer than one TPDU. ESME_RINVCMDLEN 0x00000002 generic_nack command_length, or a body of the wrong length. ESME_RINVCMDID 0x00000003 generic_nack Unsupported or undefined command_id. ESME_RINVBNDSTS 0x00000004 Response A request that the session state does not allow. ESME_RALYBND 0x00000005 Bind response A bind in a bound state. ESME_RSYSERR 0x00000008 submit_sm_resp The message could not be stored or encoded. ESME_RINVSRCADR 0x0000000A submit_sm_resp source_addr. ESME_RINVDSTADR 0x0000000B submit_sm_resp destination_addr. ESME_RBINDFAIL 0x0000000D Bind response Any refused bind. ESME_RINVSUBREP 0x00000042 submit_sm_resp replace_if_present_flag 1. ESME_RINVESMCLASS 0x00000043 submit_sm_resp esm_class. ESME_RSUBMITFAIL 0x00000045 submit_sm_resp data_coding, protocol_id, the user data header, or GSM 7-bit, IA5 or UCS2 user data. ESME_RINVSRCTON 0x00000048 submit_sm_resp source_addr_ton. ESME_RINVSRCNPI 0x00000049 submit_sm_resp source_addr_npi. ESME_RINVDSTTON 0x00000050 submit_sm_resp dest_addr_ton. ESME_RINVDSTNPI 0x00000051 submit_sm_resp dest_addr_npi. ESME_RTHROTTLED 0x00000058 submit_sm_resp Inbound window full. ESME_RINVSCHED 0x00000061 submit_sm_resp schedule_delivery_time. ESME_RINVEXPIRY 0x00000062 submit_sm_resp validity_period. ESME_RINVDFTMSGID 0x00000063 submit_sm_resp sm_default_msg_id. ESME_RINVOPTPARSTREAM 0x000000C0 Response Optional parameters that do not decode. ESME_ROPTPARNOTALLWD 0x000000C1 submit_sm_resp short_message with message_payload; sar_* or ports with UDHI. ESME_RINVPARLEN 0x000000C2 Response A field over its maximum length, or a TLV of the wrong length. ESME_RINVOPTPARAMVAL 0x000000C4 submit_sm_resp sar_* values; dest_addr_subunit against data_coding; a TLV that should be a C-Octet String and is not. ESME_RUNKNOWNERR 0x000000FF generic_nack Invalid sequence_number.

An error response has no body (§4.1.2, §4.1.4, §4.4.2), except bind_transceiver_resp, which carries system_id (Table 4-6). The SMSC logs the reason of a refused submit_sm at level debug, with the system_id.

Values the SMSC acts on in deliver_sm_resp: see Notifications.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Behaviours that SMPP 3.4 does not define:

Behaviour Where TLS from the first octet. Transport A maximum command_length of 68 KiB. Transport data_coding 0x00 is the GSM 7-bit default alphabet, unpacked. data_coding data_coding 0x02 or 0x04 with protocol_id 0x7F becomes TP-DCS 0xF6, class 2. data_coding A replace type protocol_id replaces only messages of the same ESME. protocol_id A two-digit year is within 49 years before and 50 years after the current year. Validity and scheduling A missing source_port or destination_port is port 0. User data and optional parameters Notifications go to a receiving session of the ESME that submitted the message. Notifications Receipts use data_coding 0x01. Delivery receipts A replaced message's receipt is DELETED, with done date the replacement time. Delivery receipts Receipt err is the TP-Status in decimal. Delivery receipts The SIM's answer is an SME Manual/User Acknowledgement, with receipted_message_id. SIM answers

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• SMPP 3.3 and earlier, and SMPP 5.0.
  • query_sm, replace_sm, cancel_sm, submit_multi, data_sm, alert_notification and outbind.
  • Messages from phones to ESMEs, such as a Response Packet that the SIM sends in an SMS-SUBMIT (TS 31.115 §4.2).
  • Splitting user data longer than one TPDU.
  • Scheduled delivery, the datagram and transaction modes, SME delivery acknowledgements and intermediate notifications.
  • The PROXY protocol.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
Ella SMSC runs on Linux. It supports amd64 and arm64 architectures.

Up to 1,000 subscribers Up to 100,000 subscribers CPU 1 core 4 cores Memory 1 GB RAM 8 GB RAM Disk 10 GB 100 GB Operating System Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Kernel SCTP, for Diameter SCTP, for Diameter

Each column is sized for 20 short messages per subscriber per day, kept for 30 days, with at least 7 times the busiest hour's rate to spare. The 100,000 subscriber host is the one of the performance reference.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Requests send a token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is either:

  • an access token, from log in or refresh the access token, valid for 15 minutes;
  • an API token, which starts with ellasmsc_.

These paths take no token: GET /api/v1/livez, GET /api/v1/readyz, GET /api/v1/status, GET /api/v1/metrics, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml, POST /api/v1/init, POST /api/v1/cluster/join, POST /api/v1/auth/login, /refresh and /logout, and GET /api/v1/auth/oidc, /oidc/login and /oidc/callback.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role role_id Allows Admin 1 Everything. Read Only 2 Reading messages without their content, Diameter, operator, delivery and retention settings, ESMEs, and the cluster. Network Manager 3 Read Only, plus reading message content, sending messages, updating operator, delivery and retention settings, and managing Diameter peers. Submitter 4 Sending messages, and reading the messages it sent, their content included.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users, single sign-on or ESMEs.

Only an Admin manages ESMEs. An ESME binds over SMPP with the role of its user.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Ella SMSC's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a result:

{
    "result": "Result content"
}

A failed response carries an error:

{
    "error": "Error message"
}

GET /api/v1/livez and GET /api/v1/readyz answer 204 with no body when they succeed. GET /api/v1/metrics returns text in the Prometheus exposition format, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

Times are RFC 3339, in UTC.

docs.title: OpenAPI Specification
docs.text:
The full API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella SMSC instance:

GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
• 200 - Success.
  • 201 - Created.
  • 204 - No content.
  • 400 - Bad request.
  • 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
  • 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
  • 404 - Not found.
  • 405 - Method not allowed.
  • 409 - Conflict.
  • 429 - Too many requests. Retry-After is the seconds to wait.
  • 500 - Internal server error.
  • 502 - The identity provider cannot be reached or used. See Test an identity provider.
  • 503 - Not ready. See Check readiness.

docs.title: Log In
docs.text:
This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, smsc_session, or __Host-smsc_session over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/login

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address, in any case. password string Yes Password.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Wrong email or password. 429 More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Refresh the Access Token
docs.text:
This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/refresh

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Log Out
docs.text:
This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/logout

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 204 Logged out, or no session.

docs.title: Get the Single Sign-On Option
docs.text:
This path tells the login page whether to show the button to sign in through the identity provider.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak"
    }
}

docs.title: Sign In Through the Identity Provider
docs.text:
The login page sends the browser to this path, which redirects it to the identity provider. It counts toward the login limit of 20 per minute per address.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/login

docs.title: Return From the Identity Provider
docs.text:
The identity provider sends the browser back to this path, the redirect URL. Each login completes once. On success, it sets the session cookie, for the session lifetime, and redirects to /. Otherwise, it redirects to /login?error=<error>, and the auth_oidc_login audit event gives the details.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Error Description rate_limited Too many logins from the address. unavailable Single sign-on is off, or the identity provider cannot be reached. failed The login expired, was already used or is invalid, the single sign-on settings changed during it, or the identity provider returned an error. denied The user or the identity provider refused access. not_set_up The identity provider gives no email, or no user has it and no group mapping is set. email_not_verified The identity provider marks the email as not verified, or does not say and trust_unverified_email is off. linked_elsewhere The user with the email is linked to another account at the identity provider. no_group None of the user's groups is mapped to a role. groups_overage The user is in too many groups for the identity provider to list them. too_many_users 50 users exist. error Internal error.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
A backup holds every message, user and setting, message content and the single sign-on client secret included. It leaves out the cluster's secrets: the key that signs access tokens, the single sign-on cookie key, and the key and tokens to join a node.

Both paths require Admin. Restoring requires an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Back Up
docs.text:
This path returns a backup of the database.

Method Path GET /api/v1/backup

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
A gzipped tar archive, with Content-Type: application/gzip and its file name in Content-Disposition, such as smsc-backup-20261104T120000Z.tar.gz.

File Description manifest.json Format, schema version and time of the backup. SHA256SUMS SHA-256 checksums of smsc.db and manifest.json. smsc.db The database.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
This path replaces every message, user and setting with those of a backup, on every node of a cluster, and closes the SMPP sessions. The cluster keeps its nodes and its secrets.

Method Path POST /api/v1/restore

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: An archive from Back Up, with Content-Type: application/gzip.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Backup restored successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 Not a backup, a checksum does not match, or the backup's schema is newer than this version's. 503 Not ready to restore. Retry.

docs.title: Cluster
docs.text:
A cluster is a set of Ella SMSC nodes that share their messages, users and settings. See High Availability.

Reading the cluster requires Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. The other paths, except Join a Cluster, require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Get the Cluster
docs.text:
This path returns the node that answered, its cluster, and every member.

Method Path GET /api/v1/cluster

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description node_id string ID of the node that answered. cluster_id string ID of the cluster. clustered boolean The node has a cluster block. leader_id string ID of the leader. Absent when there is none. term int Election term. applied_index int Last log entry applied by the node. commit_index int Last log entry committed by the cluster. schema int Database schema version of the cluster. healthy boolean The cluster is healthy. Absent when no leader answers. failure_tolerance int Voters that can fail without stopping writes. Absent when no leader answers. members[].node_id string ID of the member. members[].address string Cluster address of the member. members[].diameter_label string First label of the member's Diameter host: smsc- and the last 12 hex characters of node_id. members[].display_name string Display name of the member. Empty when unset. See Update a Member. members[].version string Version of the member. members[].joined_at string Time the member joined. members[].drain_state string active, draining or drained. See Drain a Member. members[].suffrage string voter, nonvoter (catching up, or standby), or none. members[].leader boolean The member is the leader. members[].healthy boolean The member is healthy. Absent when no leader answers. members[].last_contact string Time since the leader last heard from the member. members[].applied_index int Last log entry applied by the member. members[].diverged boolean The member's database differs from the leader's. Absent when it does not.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "node_id": "0199f6a2-5c1e-7d3a-9b1f-2a4c6e8d0f12",

            {

docs.title: Create a Join Token
docs.text:
This path returns a token that lets one node join the cluster, once.

Method Path POST /api/v1/cluster/tokens

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description ttl_seconds int No Validity of the token, 300 to 86400. Default 1800.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "AXsiaWQiOiI0ZjJk...",
        "expires_at": "2026-11-05T09:44:02Z"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 The token. 400 ttl_seconds is out of range. 409 The node has no cluster block. 410 The node was removed from the cluster.

docs.title: Join a Cluster
docs.text:
This path joins a node with no user and no message to a cluster. It takes no access token.

Method Path POST /api/v1/cluster/join

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description token string Yes A token from Create a Join Token.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "token": "AXsiaWQiOiI0ZjJk..."
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Joined the cluster"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 The token is not valid or expired, or the node runs an older version than the cluster. 403 The node has a user. 409 The node has a message, is already in a cluster, or has no cluster block, the token was used, or a peer has the node's Diameter host. 429 Too many attempts from the client address. 502 No member answered.

docs.title: Update a Member
docs.text:
This path sets the display name of a member.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description display_name string Yes Up to 63 bytes. Empty clears it.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "display_name": "paris-1"
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 The name is over 63 bytes. 404 No such member. 410 The node was removed from the cluster.

docs.title: Drain a Member
docs.text:
Method Path POST /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}/drain POST /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}/resume

drain sets the member's drain_state to draining, then drained. resume sets it to active.

Interface Draining or drained member Readiness Fails. SMPP Closes its sessions and refuses binds. Diameter Stays up. Leadership Moves to another voter.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No such member. 409 The member is the only member of the cluster. 410 The node was removed from the cluster.

docs.title: Remove a Member
docs.text:
This path removes a drained member from the cluster. The removed node stops serving.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/cluster/members/{node_id}

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description force boolean true removes a member that is not drained, such as one that is down for good.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No such member. 409 The member is not drained, or the cluster would lose its majority without it. 503 No leader. Retry.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text: The delivery settings set how long the SMSC attempts delivery of a message, and when it retries a failed delivery. The retention sets how long it keeps a message afterwards.

docs.title: Get the Delivery Settings
docs.text:
This path returns the delivery settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/delivery

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description default_validity_seconds int How long delivery of a message without its own validity period is attempted, in seconds. The same applies to status reports. retry_intervals_seconds array Wait before each retry, in seconds. The last interval repeats. Empty: a failed delivery is not retried.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 604800,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300, 900, 3600]
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Delivery Settings
docs.text:
This path replaces the delivery settings. The new validity applies to the messages received afterwards; the new intervals, to the next retries.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/delivery

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description default_validity_seconds int Yes 1 to 315360000 (10 years). retry_intervals_seconds array Yes Each at least 1.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
    "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "default_validity_seconds": 86400,
        "retry_intervals_seconds": [60, 300]
    }
}

docs.title: Diameter
docs.text: Configured peers are the Diameter agents that the SMSC connects to, and their routes. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Network Manager or Admin.

docs.title: Get the Diameter Status
docs.text:
This path returns the Diameter identity of the SMSC, its peers, and its routes.

Method Path GET /api/v1/diameter

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description host string Origin-Host of the SMSC. realm string Origin-Realm of the SMSC. peers array Connected and configured peers. peers[].id int ID of a configured peer. peers[].configured boolean Whether the peer is configured. peers[].host string Origin-Host of the peer. peers[].realm string Origin-Realm of the peer. peers[].address string Remote address of the connection. peers[].state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. peers[].applications array Applications the peer supports: s6c, sgd. peers[].since string Time of the last state change. peers[].error string Last connection error of a configured peer. routes array The s6c route to the HSS, then the routes of the configured peers, default routes last. routes[].realm string Destination-Realm. Empty for a default route. routes[].default boolean Whether the route is a default route. routes[].application string s6c or sgd. routes[].peers array Hosts of the open peers of the route.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "host": "smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "peers": [
            {
                "configured": false,
                "host": "core.example.org",
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "address": "127.0.0.1",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:46:07.330Z"
            },
            {
                "id": 1,
                "configured": true,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                "address": "192.0.2.10",
                "state": "open",
                "applications": ["sgd", "s6c"],
                "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
            }
        ],
        "routes": [
            {
                "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "default": false,
                "application": "s6c",
                "peers": ["core.example.org"]
            },
            {
                "realm": "",
                "default": true,
                "application": "sgd",
                "peers": ["dea1.ipx.example.net"]
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: List Peers
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/diameter/peers

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 1,
                "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
                "port": 3868,
                "routes": [
                    { "default": true, "application": "sgd", "priority": 0 }
                ],
                "status": {
                    "state": "open",
                    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
                    "realm": "ipx.example.net",
                    "since": "2026-10-27T18:47:12.004Z"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Create a Peer
docs.text: Method Path POST /api/v1/diameter/peers

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description host string No Origin-Host the peer must give. Empty accepts any. addresses array Yes IP addresses of the peer. A peer with a host must connect from one of them. port int No Default 3868. routes array No Routes of the peer. routes[].realm string Unless default Destination-Realm, e.g. epc.mnc002.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org. routes[].default boolean No Default route: every realm without another route, except the SMSC's own. sgd only, without realm. routes[].application string Yes sgd or s6c. An s6c route takes the SMSC's own realm. routes[].priority int No Lowest first; equal priorities share the load. Default 0.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "host": "dea1.ipx.example.net",
    "addresses": ["192.0.2.10", "198.51.100.10"],
    "routes": [
        { "default": true, "application": "sgd" },
        { "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org", "application": "s6c" }
    ]
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 The peer, with its id. 400 Invalid peer. 409 host is another peer's or the SMSC's, or two peers without a host share an address.

docs.title: Get a Peer
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
The fields of the request body, plus:

Field Type Description id int ID of the peer. status object Connection to the peer. Absent until the SMSC applies the peer, and from the responses to create and update. status.state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. status.host string Origin-Host the peer gave. status.realm string Origin-Realm the peer gave. status.since string Time of the last state change. status.error string Last connection error.

docs.title: Update a Peer
docs.text:
The request body is that of Create a Peer. A change of host, addresses or port reconnects.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}

docs.title: Delete a Peer
docs.text: Method Path DELETE /api/v1/diameter/peers/{id}

docs.title: ESMEs
docs.text:
An ESME account is what an External Short Message Entity, such as an OTA platform, binds to the SMPP listener with, with at most 4 sessions at once. It acts as its user: the messages it submits are the user's, and the user's role decides which binds it may make. See Binds.

Reading ESMEs requires Admin, Read Only or Network Manager. Creating, updating and deleting them requires Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: List ESMEs
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/esmes

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description system_id string The system_id the ESME binds with. user string Email of the user the ESME acts as. allowed_networks array IP prefixes the ESME may bind from. created_at string Time the ESME was created. sessions array Bound sessions, oldest first. sessions[].bind_type string transmitter, receiver or transceiver. sessions[].remote_address string Address and port of the client. sessions[].bound_at string Time of the bind.

The password is never returned.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "system_id": "ota",
                "user": "ota@example.com",
                "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
                "sessions": [
                    {
                        "bind_type": "transceiver",
                        "remote_address": "10.1.0.5:40312",
                        "bound_at": "2026-10-27T18:41:55.906Z"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Create an ESME
docs.text:
At most 50 ESMEs. Without a password, the SMSC generates one of 8 letters and digits, and returns it as password in this response only.

Method Path POST /api/v1/esmes

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description system_id string Yes 1 to 15 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1). user string Yes Email of an existing user, the user the ESME acts as. password string No 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters (SMPP 3.4 §4.1.1). Default: generated. allowed_networks array No IP prefixes, such as 10.1.0.0/24 or 2001:db8::/64, at most 50. Default: none, which allows no address.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "system_id": "ota",
    "user": "ota@example.com",
    "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"]
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "system_id": "ota",
        "user": "ota@example.com",
        "allowed_networks": ["10.1.0.0/24"],
        "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:40:02.118Z",
        "sessions": [],
        "password": "q7Rk2LxW"
    }
}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 The ESME, with the generated password when none was given. 400 Invalid field, no user with the email, or 50 ESMEs exist. 409 An ESME has the system_id.

docs.title: Get an ESME
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/esmes/{system_id}

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description system_id string The system_id of the ESME, URL-encoded.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No ESME has this system_id.

docs.title: Update an ESME
docs.text:
This path replaces the allowed networks of an ESME, and its password when one is given, and closes its sessions, which bind again under the new settings. The system_id and the user cannot be changed.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/esmes/{system_id}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description password string No 1 to 8 printable ASCII characters. Without it, the password stays. allowed_networks array Yes As in Create an ESME.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 The ESME. 400 Invalid field. 404 No ESME has this system_id.

docs.title: Delete an ESME
docs.text:
This path deletes an ESME, closes its sessions, and drops the receipts and SIM answers not yet sent to it. Its messages stay, as its user's. Deleting the user deletes its ESMEs.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/esmes/{system_id}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "ESME deleted successfully"
    }
}

docs.title: Initialize Ella SMSC
docs.text:
This path creates the first user, an Admin, and logs it in.

Method Path POST /api/v1/init

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address. password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 403 A user exists. 429 Too many attempts from the client address.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "correct horse"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "System initialized successfully",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
A message is a short message the SMSC received, from a phone, from the API, or from an ESME over SMPP, with its delivery status and the status reports the SMSC returned to the phone that sent it. A text longer than one short message is split into parts, one message each.

Responses carry no content. Get the content of a message returns it, and logs an audit event.

docs.title: Create a Message
docs.text:
This path submits a text message, or a binary message, to a phone. It returns one message per part.

Method Path POST /api/v1/messages

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
Field Type Required Description from string Yes Shown to the recipient as the sender. An E.164 number with +, or a name of 1 to 11 ASCII letters and digits, with single spaces between words, that is not all digits, such as EllaSMSC. A value without + is a name, delivered as given. to string Yes E.164 number with + of the recipient. text string One of text and binary Not empty. GSM-7 if every character is in the GSM 7-bit default alphabet or its extension table, else UCS-2. Up to 255 parts. binary object One of text and binary TPDU parameters of one short message, delivered unchanged. binary.protocol_identifier int No TP-PID (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.9), 0 to 255. Default 0. Not 32 to 62, telematic interworking. 65 to 71, replace types 1 to 7, replace the pending message of the same type from the same from, submitted by the same user; never a message from a phone or an ESME. 72, device triggering, needs an application port addressing information element in user_data_header. binary.data_coding_scheme int Yes TP-DCS (TS 23.038 §4), 0 to 255. Not a GSM 7-bit, UCS2 or reserved coding. Message class 2 when protocol_identifier is 124, ANSI-136 R-DATA, or 127, (U)SIM data download. binary.user_data_header string No TP-UDH (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.24) in hexadecimal, its length octet included. binary.user_data string Yes TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal. May be empty. At most 140 octets with user_data_header. Not split into parts. validity_seconds int No How long delivery is attempted, 1 to 315360000 (10 years). Default: the default validity of the delivery settings.

A message from the API never asks for status reports.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 A field is missing or invalid, both or neither of text and binary, the text needs more than 255 parts, or the binary user data is over 140 octets.

docs.title: Sample Request (Binary)
docs.text:
{
    "from": "+15550001000",
    "to": "+15551230002",
    "binary": {
        "protocol_identifier": 127,
        "data_coding_scheme": 246,
        "user_data_header": "027000",
        "user_data": "0011223344"
    }
}

docs.title: List Messages
docs.text:
This path returns the list of messages, most recent first. For a Submitter, only the messages it sent.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description to query str 1 to 15 digits, after an optional + Recipient: the numbers that contain these digits. +1555123 and 1555123 match +15551230002, and so does 0002. from query str 1 to 15 digits, after an optional +, or a name as in Create a Message Sender: the numbers that contain these digits, or the name, in any case. status query str pending, delivered, failed, expired, replaced Status. start query str RFC 3339 time Created at or after. end query str RFC 3339 time, not before start Created before. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id int Message identifier. from string Sender: the MSISDN of the phone, an E.164 number with +, the from of the API request, or the source_addr of the submit_sm, with + when international. to string Recipient, an E.164 number with +. encoding string gsm7, ucs2 or binary. concatenation object Present for a part of a longer message. concatenation.reference int Reference shared by the parts of the message. concatenation.part int Number of this part, from 1. concatenation.total int Number of parts. status string See Statuses. created_at string Time the SMSC received the message. updated_at string Time of the last change. expires_at string End of the validity period. next_attempt_at string Time of the next delivery attempt. Present while pending. status_report object Status reports on the message. status_report.requested boolean Whether the phone that sent the message asked for status reports. status_report.reports array Status reports the SMSC returned to that phone, oldest first. status_report.reports[].id int Status report identifier. status_report.reports[].tp_status int TP-Status the report gives (TS 23.040 §9.2.3.15). status_report.reports[].tp_status_name string Meaning of tp_status, e.g. received, replaced, no_response, validity_period_expired. status_report.reports[].status string Delivery of the report to the phone: pending, delivered, failed or expired. status_report.reports[].created_at string Time the SMSC made the report. status_report.reports[].updated_at string Time of the last change. status_report.reports[].expires_at string End of the report's validity period. status_report.reports[].next_attempt_at string Time of the next delivery attempt of the report. Present while pending. submitted_by string Email of the user that sent the message over the API, or of the user of the ESME that sent it over SMPP. Absent for a message from a phone. system_id string system_id of the ESME that sent the message over SMPP. Absent for other messages, and once the ESME is deleted.

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text: Status When pending Not yet delivered, within its validity period. delivered A serving node took it. failed The recipient is unknown, is not allowed SMS, or has no serving node that supports SGd. failed The network rejected the recipient's subscription or phone as illegal. failed The SIM refused a (U)SIM data download message. failed An attempt failed, and the message is single-shot or retries are off. expired Its validity period ended before its delivery. replaced A later message of the same replace type, from the same sender and submitter, before its delivery: the same phone, user or ESME.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 4,
                "from": "+15550001000",
                "to": "+15551230001",
                "encoding": "gsm7",
                "concatenation": {
                    "reference": 74,
                    "part": 2,
                    "total": 2
                },
                "status": "pending",
                "created_at": "2026-10-27T18:53:37.120Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-10-27T18:54:07.151Z",
                "expires_at": "2026-11-03T18:53:37.120Z",
                "next_attempt_at": "2026-10-27T18:55:07.151Z",
                "status_report": {
                    "requested": false,
                    "reports": []
                }
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 1,
        "total_count": 3
    }
}

docs.title: Count Messages
docs.text:
This path returns the number of messages in each status. For a Submitter, only the messages it sent.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/counts

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description start query str RFC 3339 time Created at or after. end query str RFC 3339 time, not before start Created before.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description pending int Messages pending. See Statuses. delivered int Messages delivered. failed int Messages failed. expired int Messages expired. replaced int Messages replaced.

docs.title: Get the Content of a Message
docs.text:
This path returns the content of a message, and logs an audit event read_message_content with the email of the caller. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found. A Read Only user cannot read content.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/content

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description id int Message identifier.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description text string Text of the part. Absent for a binary message. binary object TPDU parameters of a binary message. binary.protocol_identifier int TP-PID. binary.data_coding_scheme int TP-DCS. binary.user_data_header string TP-UDH in hexadecimal, its length octet included. Absent when there is none. binary.user_data string TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal. deliver_reports array SMS-DELIVER-REPORTs (TS 23.040 §9.2.2.1a) the serving nodes passed on, oldest first. Absent when there are none. deliver_reports[].attempt_id int Delivery attempt of the report: in the RP-ACK when its outcome is success, else in the RP-ERROR. deliver_reports[].tpdu string The report in hexadecimal. The other deliver_reports[] fields are absent when it does not decode. deliver_reports[].protocol_identifier int TP-PID, when present. deliver_reports[].data_coding_scheme int TP-DCS, when present. deliver_reports[].user_data_header string TP-UDH in hexadecimal, when present. deliver_reports[].user_data string TP-UD after the header, in hexadecimal, when present.

docs.title: List Delivery Attempts
docs.text:
This path returns the routing and delivery attempts of a message, oldest first. For a Submitter, a message it did not send is not found.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/attempts

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description id int Message identifier.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description id int Attempt identifier. started_at string Start of the attempt. completed_at string End of the attempt. step string routing: a routing lookup at the HSS, over S6c. delivery: a delivery to a serving node, over SGd. node string Host of the HSS that answered the routing lookup, or of the serving node. node_type string Type of the serving node: mme, sgsn, ip_sm_gw, smsf_3gpp or smsf_non_3gpp. outcome string success; no_hss, no HSS connected; unreachable, the serving node not connected; timeout, no answer in time; the error the node gave: user_unknown, absent_user, user_busy_for_mt_sms, facility_not_supported, illegal_user, illegal_equipment, sm_delivery_failure, service_not_subscribed, service_barred, mwd_list_full; diameter_error, another error answer; or error. result_code int Result-Code or Experimental-Result-Code of the answer. vendor_id int Vendor-Id of an Experimental-Result-Code. failure_cause string SM-Delivery-Failure-Cause of an sm_delivery_failure. tp_failure_cause string TP-Failure-Cause the phone gave. absent_user_diagnostics object Why the phone is unreachable, by node: mme, msc, sgsn, ip_sm_gw, smsf_3gpp, smsf_non_3gpp.

docs.title: Get Metrics
docs.text:
This path returns the metrics of the SMSC in the Prometheus exposition format, negotiated from the request's Accept header. See Observability for the list.

Method Path GET /api/v1/metrics

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
# HELP ellasmsc_hss_peers Open Diameter peers in the operator's realm that serve S6c, which the SMSC asks to route messages. At 0, messages to phones wait.
# TYPE ellasmsc_hss_peers gauge
ellasmsc_hss_peers 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_pending Short messages and status reports waiting for delivery, by type (message, status_report) and state: due (to be delivered now, or being delivered) or waiting (for a retry or for the phone to be reachable). Due messages that stay due mean the deliverer is falling behind.
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_pending gauge
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="message"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="due",type="status_report"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="message"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_pending{state="waiting",type="status_report"} 0
# HELP ellasmsc_messages_received_total Short messages received, one per TPDU, by origin (mobile, api) and result (accepted, rejected, error).
# TYPE ellasmsc_messages_received_total counter
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="accepted"} 2
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="api",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="accepted"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="error"} 0
ellasmsc_messages_received_total{origin="mobile",result="rejected"} 0

docs.title: Single Sign-On
docs.text: These paths configure sign-in to the UI through an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider. They require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Get the OIDC Settings
docs.text:
This path never returns the client secret.

Method Path GET /api/v1/oidc

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description enabled boolean Users can sign in through the identity provider. external_url string The URL users reach Ella SMSC at. redirect_url string The redirect URL to register at the identity provider. Empty without an external URL. issuer string The identity provider's issuer URL. client_id string The client ID registered at the identity provider. client_secret_set boolean A client secret is stored. display_name string The name on the login button. scopes array The scopes requested. Initially openid, email and profile. session_lifetime_seconds int How long a session started through the identity provider lasts. Initially 86400. trust_unverified_email boolean Email addresses are accepted when the identity provider does not send email_verified. An email_verified of false is always refused. ca_certificate string PEM certificates the identity provider's TLS certificate must chain to. Empty: the system's. groups_claim string The claim, in the ID token or UserInfo, that holds the user's groups. group_roles array Group-to-role mappings, in order.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "external_url": "https://smsc.example.com",
        "redirect_url": "https://smsc.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback",
        "issuer": "https://idp.example.com/realms/smsc",
        "client_id": "smsc",
        "client_secret_set": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak",
        "scopes": ["openid", "email", "profile"],
        "session_lifetime_seconds": 86400,
        "trust_unverified_email": false,
        "ca_certificate": "",
        "groups_claim": "groups",
        "group_roles": [
            {"group": "smsc-admins", "role_id": 1},
            {"group": "noc", "role_id": 3}
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Update the OIDC Settings
docs.text:
This path replaces the settings, which take effect at once. Disabling OIDC or changing the issuer ends all sessions started through the identity provider.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/oidc

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description enabled boolean Yes external_url string When enabled An https URL with no path. Stored as https://host[:port]. issuer string When enabled An https URL with no query or fragment, as the identity provider gives it. client_id string When enabled At most 255 characters. client_secret string When enabled and none is stored, or when issuer or client_id changes At most 255 characters. Empty or absent: the stored secret is kept. display_name string When enabled At most 64 characters. scopes array Yes At most 20, including openid and email. session_lifetime_seconds int Yes 300 to 2592000 (30 days). trust_unverified_email boolean No Default false. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates. groups_claim string With group_roles The claim name, such as groups. group_roles array No At most 100 objects with a group, matched exactly, and a role_id, 1 to 4. Each group at most once.

docs.title: Group Roles
docs.text: group_roles At each login through the identity provider Empty An Admin sets the role. Someone with no user in Ella SMSC is refused. Not empty The first mapping whose group the user is in sets the role. A user in none is refused. Someone with no user in Ella SMSC gets one, with that role. A pinned role is kept, whatever the groups. The last Admin with a password stays Admin.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 Updated. The response holds the new settings. 400 Invalid field, or issuer or client_id changes without a client_secret.

docs.title: Test an Identity Provider
docs.text:
This path checks that Ella SMSC can use an identity provider. It changes no setting.

Method Path POST /api/v1/oidc/discovery

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description issuer string Yes The issuer URL to test. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates to trust for the provider.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description issuer string The provider's issuer. authorization_endpoint string token_endpoint string token_endpoint_auth_method string client_secret_basic or client_secret_post: how Ella SMSC sends the client secret. userinfo_endpoint string Empty if the provider has none. jwks_uri string signing_algorithms array The algorithms the provider signs ID tokens with. keys int The number of signing keys. pkce boolean The provider supports PKCE. issuer_parameter boolean The provider supports RFC 9207.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 The provider can be used. 400 Invalid issuer or CA certificate. 502 The provider cannot be reached or cannot be used, for example because its token endpoint supports neither client_secret_basic nor client_secret_post. The error says why.

docs.title: Operator
docs.text: The operator is the PLMN of the SMSC, from which its Diameter identity derives, its service centre address, and the numbering plan that converts the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers.

docs.title: Get the Operator
docs.text:
This path returns the operator settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcc string Mobile Country Code. mnc string Mobile Network Code. service_centre_address string E.164 number of the SMSC, which phones have as SMSC number. numbering object Conversion of the numbers phones send to E.164 numbers. numbering.country_code string Country code, added to the numbers phones send in national format. numbering.national_prefix string Prefix that phones dial before a national number, removed before the country code is added. Empty if none. numbering.international_prefix string Prefix that phones dial before an international number, removed. Empty if none.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Operator
docs.text:
This path replaces the operator settings. A change of MCC or MNC changes the Diameter host and realm: the SMSC restarts Diameter, and its peers reconnect.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description mcc string Yes 3 digits. mnc string Yes 2 or 3 digits. service_centre_address string Yes E.164 number with +, e.g. +15550000000. numbering object Yes numbering.country_code string Yes 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0. numbering.national_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. Differs from international_prefix unless empty. numbering.international_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011"
    }
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "service_centre_address": "+15550000000",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Pprof
docs.text: These paths serve the net/http/pprof API. They require Admin, and accept an API token.

docs.title: Profiling Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/pprof/ An HTML page listing the available profiles. GET /api/v1/pprof/allocs A sampling of all past memory allocations. GET /api/v1/pprof/cmdline The command line invocation of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutine Stack traces of all current goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak Stack traces of all leaked goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/heap A sampling of memory allocations of live objects. GET /api/v1/pprof/profile A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default. GET /api/v1/pprof/threadcreate Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. GET /api/v1/pprof/trace An execution trace, of 1 second by default. GET, POST /api/v1/pprof/symbol Function names of program counters.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Paths Description seconds profile, trace Duration of the capture. seconds allocs, goroutine, heap Returns the difference of the profile over this duration. debug allocs, goroutine, heap, threadcreate 0: protobuf. 1: text. 2 (goroutine): stack traces in the format of a panic. gc heap 1: runs a garbage collection first.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: The retention sets how long the SMSC keeps a message once it has its final status: delivered, failed, expired or replaced. The SMSC then deletes it, with its status reports and delivery attempts, within the hour. It keeps a message until its status reports, too, have had their final status for that long.

docs.title: Get the Retention
docs.text:
This path returns the retention.

Method Path GET /api/v1/messages/retention

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description days int Days a message is kept once it has its final status. Default: 30.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "days": 30
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Retention
docs.text:
This path replaces the retention. It applies from the next deletion, within the hour.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/messages/retention

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description days int Yes At least 1.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "days": 7
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "days": 7
    }
}

docs.title: Get the Status
docs.text:
This path returns the version of the SMSC, whether it is initialized, and the identity of the node that answered.

Method Path GET /api/v1/status

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description version string Version. revision string Git commit of the build. Empty in development builds. initialized boolean Whether the first user exists. See Initialize. clustered boolean Whether the configuration file has a cluster block. node_id string ID of the node that answered. display_name string Display name of the node. Empty when unset. See Update a Member. diameter_label string First label of the node's Diameter host: smsc- and the last 12 hex characters of node_id.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "version": "v0.0.1",
        "revision": "79194832364de9583e8e659ba700c2fa9ba1e351",
        "initialized": true,
        "clustered": false,
        "node_id": "01a1ac75-e354-762b-b38f-013c0a7ca824",
        "display_name": "",
        "diameter_label": "smsc-013c0a7ca824"
    }
}

docs.title: Check Liveness
docs.text:
This path answers while the process serves HTTP.

Method Path GET /api/v1/livez

It answers 204 No Content.

docs.title: Check Readiness
docs.text:
This path returns whether the SMSC can serve requests: its database answers, it is not shutting down, and, in a cluster, it is not draining and is in contact with the leader.

Method Path GET /api/v1/readyz

It answers 204 No Content when ready, and 503 Service Unavailable otherwise:

{
    "error": "Not ready"
}

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Paths under /api/v1/users/me act on the user of the token. The others require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Get My User
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users/me

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "email": "admin@example.com",
        "role_id": 1,
        "role_pinned": false,
        "password_set": true,
        "oidc_linked": false
    }
}

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description email string Email address. role_id int 1 to 4. See roles. role_pinned boolean The role is kept whatever the user's groups. password_set boolean The user has a password. oidc_linked boolean The user is linked to an account at the current identity provider.

The other paths that return users return the same fields.

docs.title: Update My Password
docs.text:
This path ends the user's other sessions. It requires an access token.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/me/password

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description current_password string Yes Current password. password string Yes New password, 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 Wrong current password, or invalid new password. 409 The user has no password. 429 More than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account, counting failed logins.

docs.title: List Users
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {

docs.title: Create a User
docs.text:
At most 50 users.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address. ASCII letters are stored in lower case. password string No 8 to 72 bytes. Without it, the user signs in only through the identity provider. role_id int Yes 1 to 4. See roles. role_pinned boolean No Keep the role whatever the user's groups. Default false.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 400 Invalid field, or 50 users exist. 409 A user has the email, in any case.

docs.title: Get a User
docs.text: Method Path GET /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Update a User
docs.text:
This path sets the role of a user. A role change ends the user's sessions and the SMPP sessions of its ESMEs. An Admin cannot change its own role, and the last Admin with a password stays an Admin.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description role_id int Yes 1 to 4. role_pinned boolean No Keep the role whatever the user's groups. Without it, the current value is kept.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The role comes from the user's groups and role_pinned is not true, or the user is the last Admin with a password.

docs.title: Update a User's Password
docs.text:
This path ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot update its own password here.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/users/{email}/password

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description password string Yes 8 to 72 bytes.

docs.title: Remove a User's Password
docs.text:
This path removes the password of a user, who can then sign in only through the identity provider. It ends the user's sessions. An Admin cannot remove its own password, and the last Admin with a password keeps it.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/password

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The user has no password, or is the last Admin with a password.

docs.title: Unlink a User
docs.text:
This path unlinks a user from their account at the identity provider, and ends the sessions started through it. Their next login through the identity provider links them again by email. An Admin cannot unlink itself.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}/oidc

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 404 No user has the email, or the user is not linked to the current identity provider.

docs.title: Delete a User
docs.text:
This path deletes the user with its sessions, API tokens and ESMEs. An Admin cannot delete itself, and the last Admin with a password cannot be deleted.

Method Path DELETE /api/v1/users/{email}

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 409 The user is the last Admin with a password.

docs.title: Create an API Token
docs.text:
This path returns the token, the only time it is shown. At most 12 per user. Requires an access token.

Method Path POST /api/v1/users/me/api-tokens POST /api/v1/users/{email}/api-tokens

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes 3 to 50 characters, unique among the user's tokens. expires_at string No RFC 3339 time in the future. Without it, the token does not expire.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 201 Created. 400 Invalid field, or 12 tokens exist. 409 The user has a token of that name.

In this tutorial, we will add SMS to a private 5G network with Ella SMSC.

Tutorial Hardware Required Installation Method Duration Send Your First SMS An Ella Core 5G network, two phones Snap ~15 min

docs.title: Send Your First SMS
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add Ella SMSC to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and send an SMS between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 15 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need:

  • A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware) tutorial, with PLMN 00101.
  • Two phones attached to the network, with SIM cards whose SMSC number you can set.

docs.title: 1. Install Ella SMSC
docs.text:
On the host running Ella Core, install and start the Ella SMSC snap:

sudo snap install ella-smsc
sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd

docs.title: 2. Initialize Ella SMSC
docs.text:
Open your browser at http://<host-ip>:5010. The Initialize Ella SMSC page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click Create.

The Diameter page shows no connected peers yet.

docs.title: 3. Connect Ella Core
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to Operator and scroll to the SMS section.

Click Add Service Center and set:

  • Address: 127.0.0.1
  • Numbers: +15550000000
  • Diameter Identity: the Host of Ella SMSC's Diameter page, e.g. smsc-013c0a7ca824.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org

Click Add. The service center shows Connected.

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Diameter. Under Connected Peers, Ella Core shows open, with HSS set to yes.

docs.title: 4. Give the subscribers an MSISDN
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, for each of the two subscribers:

  • Go to Subscribers and open the subscriber.
  • In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to MSISDN.
  • Enter +15551230001 for the first subscriber and +15551230002 for the second, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Set the SMSC number on the SIM cards
docs.text: On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to +15550000000.

docs.title: 6. Send an SMS
docs.text:
From the first phone, send hello to +15551230002. The second phone receives it.

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to Messages. The message shows delivered. Click it to see its routing and delivery attempts.

You have added SMS to your 5G network.

docs.text:

  • Send messages from an application.
